note: Level and how-to-use guidance for the 71 resources. Level describes how much background a resource assumes, not its importance. foundation = plain-language, no background needed; core = practical, builds on this week's foundations; deep = standards and specifications, to be used as reference.

levels.foundation: Start here. Plain language, no background needed.
levels.core: Practical. Builds on the foundations of the week.
levels.deep: Reference. Standards and specifications: skim, look things up, return later.

suggestedDayChanges.reason: Your plan puts threat-model vocabulary on Day 4, after you have seen Keycloak.
Governance material is easier after the week's hands-on work; keep it optional.
Read it after the Day 11 attack lab, when the attacks have names you recognize.
Optional reference after you have used the authorization-code flow.

w1-keycloak-docker.howToUse: Day 1: read it through and run the Docker check only. Day 3: follow it to create your first realm and user.

w1-messer-iam.howToUse: These videos are exam prep, so listen for the concepts (who you are, what you may do, what is recorded) and ignore the exam tips and acronyms you do not need yet.

w1-tmm.howToUse: Short and conceptual. Read it after you have seen Keycloak, so the ideas have something to attach to.

w1-shostack.howToUse: Read or watch for the big picture. Pause to put each idea in your own words and add new terms to your glossary. You do not need to remember details.

w1-keycloak-admin.howToUse: Reference. Do not read it end to end. Open it when Exercise 1 uses a word you do not know (realm, role, group) and read only that section.

w1-tailscale-quickstart.howToUse: Read or watch for the big picture. Pause to put each idea in your own words and add new terms to your glossary. You do not need to remember details.

w1-1password-admin.howToUse: Search for it: no verified link yet. Look for what an admin must set up first (people, groups, sign-in rules).

w1-okta-admin.howToUse: Search for it: no verified link yet. Same question as the others: what must an admin do on day one?

w2-oauthcom.howToUse: This is the friendliest OAuth explainer. Take the three days slowly, draw each flow as boxes and arrows, and do not move on until you can say who talks to whom.

w2-rfc7636.howToUse: Reference. Read only the abstract and the introduction to understand what PKCE protects against. Optional.

w2-rfc9700.howToUse: Reference. Read after the attack lab, when each attack has a name you recognize. Skim the section titles and read two attacks properly.

w2-oidc.howToUse: Read after OAuth Simplified. The one idea to keep: OAuth is about permission to access things; OpenID Connect adds who the user is.

w2-ps-oauth.howToUse: Hard at first. Do the first two labs and read the hints freely; the goal is to see an attack happen once, not to finish every lab.
